service.description: The rail and the user's settings: the accounts (mantle.party.CommunicationServices.get#InboxUnreadCounts: the Internal account first, each mail account with its folders by kind and path, labels, identities, unread, draft and Outbox counts, and its sync state: syncing while its sync lock holds, a warning when its sign-in or its last sync failed), the mailboxes the user is in or asked to join with their unread counts, the saved searches, the Unified, Drafts and Outbox totals, me (the user, party and own addresses) and the Inbox preferences (reading pane, pane sizes, the rail collapsed, archive opens next, mark read after seconds, the undo-send seconds, threads or messages, the default account, signature placement, the two phone swipe actions, the trusted senders, and remoteImages: always shows the pictures of every sender, Commons Preferences' Mail box). Each mail account has usedBytes and storageText: the bytes its files use under dbresource://email/, sized the way FileServices sizes a drive (ec.resource.getTreeSize). Mail has no quota of its own, so the line is the size only. A part that fails is named in failedParts and logged; the rest is answered. A size that cannot be read is logged and that account's line is left out.

parameter.name: outOfOfficeList
parameter.description: The accounts whose automatic reply is on now ({emailAccountId, accountName}), for the Inbox's out-of-office banner

service.description: Remote images of a sender shown at once from now on (or not, with remove): the user preference MAIL_TRUSTED_SENDERS, a JSON list of addresses in lower case.

A page of the thread list (mantle.party.CommunicationServices.find#InboxThreads) for a view of the rail: inbox (the Unified inbox), flagged, snoozed, scheduled, drafts, sent, archive, junk, trash, outbox and all over the user's mail and internal messages (each view reads the stores it has), with emailAccountId one account's (and emailFolderId one folder, emailLabelId one label); internal, internalSent, internalArchive and comments the Internal account's; contactListId a mailbox's. A search (searchText, with Gmail's operators) is a view of all mail and messages, or of the account, Internal account or mailbox open, unless it names an in:. MAIL_CONVERSATION messages lists the mail one message at a time (threadMode false); threads, the default, keeps a thread as one row. Internal rows stay threads either way. The rows are find#InboxThreads' with its cursor and stores; termList is the search's operators for the query chips. conversationView is the mode this page used.

parameter.name: findView
parameter.description: The view find#InboxThreads was asked for

service.description: The parties the user may see with these email addresses (case does not matter): a current email of a directory party or of one of the user's personal contacts (another user's personal contacts never: IronStone R7), or a user's address. partyMap is the address in lower case to {partyId, name, isPrivate, isUser}.

The records communication events are filed on that the user may see (ironstone.shared.ChatterServices.get#RecordInfo, under the user's filters, IronStone R28): their own joins (order, request, work effort, wiki page), the generic CommunicationEventRecord and a party's _NA_ row. linkMap is the event id to [{recordEntityName, recordId, title, typeLabel, url, icon}].

The invitation a message carries (an iMIP text/calendar part or .ics file, IronStone design §12 ImipCard), read by the framework's ICalendar tool: {method, uid, summary, start, end, allDay, location, organizer, attendeeCount, emailMessageAttachmentId, workEffortId (the event on the user's calendar by its UID, when there is one), myStatus (accepted, tentative, declined or needsAction)}, or null without one or without the tool. A file that does not parse is logged and no card shows.

The thread of the reading pane, oldest message first: mail through org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.get#Thread, internal messages and mailbox posts through mantle.party.CommunicationServices.get#InternalThread (each "not found" for a thread the user may not see). Each message has its sender and recipients (with the party the address or id is, when the user may see it), date, HTML or text body, attachments (inline ones in cidMap by Content-ID), its flags and its links: the records it is filed on (get#CommEventLinks) and, for mail, the invitation it carries and how it may be unsubscribed. The thread has the union of the links, its labels and what the user may do: reply (canReply), send from its account (canSend), moderate (a mailbox's owner or moderator: Close thread).

The file of an attachment the user may read: a mail attachment (EmailMessageAttachment) of a message get#Thread shows the user, or an internal message's file (CommunicationEventContent) of a message get#InternalThread shows the user. Anything else is "not found". inlineAllowed is true for an image or a PDF.

An action on threads (a list's selection, a row's hover action, the reading pane's bar), each target by its store: {store, threadId, emailMessageId or communicationEventId (one message instead of the thread)}. Actions: read, unread, flag (the thread's newest message, or the message), unflag, archive, unarchive, trash (mail to its Trash; an internal thread is archived, as internal messages have no trash), deleteForever (mail in Trash), spam and notSpam (mail), snooze (snoozedThruDate) and unsnooze, move (emailFolderId; mail only, internal messages have no folders), labels (addLabelIdList and removeLabelIdList; mail through apply#Labels, an internal thread through set#InternalMessageLabels, each label of that store's account), close and reopen (a mailbox thread, for its owners and moderators). Mail goes through org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices (set#MessageFlags, archive#Messages, trash#Messages, report#Spam, snooze#Messages, move#Messages, apply#Labels), internal messages through mantle.party.CommunicationServices.set#InternalMessageState, set#InternalMessageLabels and close#ListThread; each checks the user's access, and a target the user does not reach is "not found". Each target is changed in a transaction of its own: one that is refused or fails is named in failedList with why, and the others are changed.

parameter.name: targetsJson
parameter.description: The targets as JSON, from a form

service.description: A bulk action on every thread of a view ("all N in this view"): the view's threads by find#InboxRows (the same parameters as the list, at most 5000), then set#ThreadState on them.

actions.script: const targets = [] let cursor = null for (let page = 0; page < 25; page++) { const out = ec.service.sync().name('ironstone.comms.InboxServices.find#InboxRows').parameters({view: view, emailAccountId: emailAccountId, emailFolderId: emailFolderId, emailLabelId: emailLabelId, contactListId: contactListId, searchText: searchText, unreadOnly: unreadOnly, cursor: cursor, pageSize: 200}).call() if (ec.message.hasError()) return for (const row of Array.from(out.threadList || [])) targets.push({store: row.store, threadId: row.threadId, lastEmailMessageId: row.lastEmailMessageId ?? null, lastCommEventId: row.lastCommEventId ?? null}) cursor = out.nextCursor if (!out.hasMore || !cursor || targets.length >= 5000) break } threadCount = targets.length updatedCount = 0 failedList = [] if (targets.length === 0) return const out = ec.service.sync().name('ironstone.comms.InboxServices.set#ThreadState').parameters({targetList: targets.slice(0, 5000), action: action, snoozedThruDate: snoozedThruDate, emailFolderId: targetEmailFolderId, addLabelIdList: addLabelIdList, removeLabelIdList: removeLabelIdList}).call() if (ec.message.hasError()) return updatedCount = out.updatedCount failedList = out.failedList

service.description: The records a message may be filed on, for the LinkToRecord dialog's drop-down: an id (lookup#ById: a party, order, request, task or event, invoice, shipment) and the search index (search#Universal over parties, requests, tasks, events and projects), each one the user may see, as options {value (entity|id), label}.

File a message (mail by emailMessageId, which makes its CommunicationEvent; an internal message by communicationEventId) on a record the user may see (mantle.party.CommunicationServices.link#CommunicationEventRecord, which checks both).
Take a message off a record (unlink#CommunicationEventRecord), for a message the user reads.

What a task, request or event made from a message starts with (the QuickCreate forms, design §12 CreateFromMessage): its name from the subject, its notes from the body as text, the customer from the sender, and the message as the new record's link (its CommunicationEvent, made for mail when it has none, so the new record's join holds the message). url is the QuickCreate screen with these in its query.

Who an address or party is, for the contact card of the reading pane: the party the user may see with that address (match#Addresses, R7) with its organization, email addresses and phone, the link to its contact record, and the latest threads with it (from: the address) in the Inbox; without one, the address and name to add as a contact.

The inbox-source provider of IronStone (Comms.xml shell-providers, boss.internal) for the BasicComms Inbox, MessageDetail, Compose and Home (plans/Comms-Framework.md §3.3, A3). The BasicComms screens call org.moqui.comms.InboxServices.run#Operation, which hands each operation here: IronStone answers it with its own service of that name (this file, ComposeServices, CommsHomeServices), over the mail and its internal messages and mailboxes together, so its Inbox is one list. Only the operations named here are answered (handled false for any other). Links to Commons are added: an invitation's event (eventUrl). operation accounts answers the user's Internal account, for the account lists of the mail settings.

Answer an invitation a message carries (get#InvitationCard): accept, tentative or decline. The event on the user's calendar (by its UID, the user a party of it) is answered with mantle.work.EventServices.respond#EventInvitation, which tells its organizer (a notification, or an iMIP REPLY to an organizer outside). An invitation from outside that is not on the calendar yet is added to it first, as an event of the user's default calendar with the user invited and the organizer's address in its description, and the REPLY (the ICalendar tool's, method REPLY, the user as the only attendee) goes to the organizer from the account the invitation came to.

The iMIP REPLY to an organizer outside (the ICalendar tool's, method REPLY, the user as the only attendee with the answer), sent as a reply to the invitation from the account it came to: a draft with reply.ics, then send#Draft. An account with no outgoing server sends nothing (sent false).

The header of an open mailbox (design §12 MailboxHeader): its name, description, public or private, posting policy, archived, the user's membership (member, pending request, role, delivery) and what the user may do (read, post, join, moderate, manage), and for those who may see them the members (the first ones and the count) and, for owners and moderators, the pending requests (mantle.marketing.ContactListServices get#ContactListAccess and find#ContactListParties). A mailbox the user may not see is "not found".

One message for MessageDetail (design §12): an email of an account the user reaches (get#Thread with its headers), or mail the system sent (no account: notifications, order and invoice mail) for a user of the ADMIN group, by emailMessageId; or by communicationEventId an internal message the user sees (get#InternalThread), the email of one (its emailMessageId), or another communication event the user may see (get#RecordLinkInfo's rules for a communication event, IronStone R28). Anything else is "not found". detail has the header fields, the body, the files, the communication events and records it is filed on, the raw headers, and what the user may do: open it in the Inbox (threadKey), resend it (a bounced message of an account the user may send from, or system mail for an administrator).

Save to Files: copy a message's attachments into a folder of a drive (FileServices.upload#Resource, keepBoth when the name is already there). id is one attachment (store email or internal, the same id get#MessageAttachment reads); without an id, emailMessageId or communicationEventId copies every file of that message. The message keeps its own copies. Each file stands alone: one that fails is named in failedList and the others are saved. A message the user may not read, or a folder the user may not write, is an error.
